key_insight: MME-CoF-Pro is a focused benchmark that quantifies whether video generative models maintain causal and temporal consistency (reasoning coherence) across frames by using both text and visual hints to probe model behavior.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized datasets and evaluation protocols for measuring reasoning/coherence of events in generated videos, enabling systematic detection of causal or temporal inconsistencies.
method: Curated benchmark: 303 video samples spanning 16 reasoning categories that test visual logic, temporal causality, object interactions, and other cross-frame behaviors.
Multimodal prompting: Uses combined text and visual hints to elicit and constrain model reasoning, revealing failures that appear only under specific cues.
Evaluation protocol: A reproducible scoring pipeline combining targeted automatic metrics and human-aligned judgments to measure event-level and frame-to-frame coherence.
impact: Provides practitioners a concrete tool to diagnose and compare reasoning failures in video generative models, guiding model selection, targeted training, and safer deployment by focusing on causal/temporal reliability.
visual_elements: Before/After timeline: side-by-side frame sequences showing coherent vs. incoherent event progression with annotated causal links.
Dataset breakdown chart: pie or bar chart showing the 16 categories and sample counts (303 total) to illustrate coverage.
Prompt-to-evaluation flow: diagram showing text+visual hint → generated video → automated metrics + human judgment → coherence score.
Failure case gallery: thumbnails of common reasoning errors (e.g., object teleportation, inconsistent object properties) with short captions.
paper_title: MME-CoF-Pro: Evaluating Reasoning Coherence in Video Generative Models with Text and Visual Hints
paper_authors: Yu Qi, Xinyi Xu, Ziyu Guo, Siyuan Ma, Renrui Zhang
